properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 8:56PM PDT until October 12 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding can be expected near times of high tide. For
the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet
is expected with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
around high tide at beach and harbor areas that is uncommon
with normal tidal ranges. Low lying areas will be most
susceptible, including Oceano. Enhanced beach erosion is
likely. The risk for significant damage is very low. There is
an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore. Large
secondary high tides are also expected each evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to be around 7
feet on Monday morning.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Carroll, MD; Frederick, MD
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 11:54PM EDT until October 12 at 3:00AM EDT by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...West Central Carroll County in north central Maryland...
East Central Frederick County in north central Maryland...

* WHEN...Until 300 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks, streams, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1153 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the warned area. Between
1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen in the past hour.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Union Bridge, Libertytown and Unionville.
- This includes the following Flood Prone Roads...
Main St near Little Pipe Creek in Union Bridge, Bucher John Road
at Cherry Branch, Mckinstrys Mill Road at Sams Creek, Beaver Dam
Road near Beaver Dam Creek and Simpsons Mill Road near Little
Pipe Creek.
- Visit http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood for safety information.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.description:
As low clouds begin to clear overnight, conditions for fog
development will become more favorable. Some dense fog is
possible and may result in visibility of one quarter mile or less.
Locations farther east into Ohio and farther south into northern
Kentucky could see visibility worsen through daybreak.

Motorists should be prepared for rapid changes in visibility.
Allow for greater distances between vehicles, use low beam
headlights, and allow extra time to reach your destination.

properties.areaDesc: Waters from Manasquan Inlet NJ to Little Egg Inlet NJ from 20 to 60 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 11 at 11:45PM EDT until October 12 at 12:45AM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
SMWPHI

The National Weather Service in Mount Holly NJ has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Outer waters from Manasquan Inlet to Little Egg Inlet NJ from 20 to
60 nm...

* Until 1245 AM EDT.

* At 1143 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 23 nm southeast of Garden State North Reef,
moving northeast at 40 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 8:45PM PDT until October 13 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, increased risk of rip currents and sneaker waves
expected with breaking waves up to 16 feet.

* WHERE...San Francisco, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern
Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 3 PM PDT Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical. Dangerous conditions are
forecast along the shoreline. Hazards include sneaker waves,
strong rip currents, and large breaking waves.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:46 PM
Monday 10/12, and 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 1:14 PM
Tuesday 10/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.areaDesc: Pohnpei Coastal Waters; Kosrae Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 1:29PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
As Invest 96W continues to slowly organize and strengthen north of
Kosrae/east of Pohnpei, inflow into the developing disturbance will
allow for locally heavy rainfall to develop, with over 1 inch per
hour rain rates probable from time to time. Rainfall totals will
likely be 2 to 5 inches tonight through Wednesday, with locally
higher amounts possible.

Winds will also increase as 96W strengthens, and at least isolated
wind gusts to 35 knots are possible with any heavy shower or
thunderstorm that develops.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues. Also keep up to date with the latest
information from your local emergency management agency.

NWSheadline: LOCALLY HEAVY RAINFALL AND GUSTY WINDS TONIGHT THROUGH WEDNESDAY, POSSIBLY LONGER

properties.description:
* WHAT...A moderate risk for sneaker waves is expected. Short
period north-northwest wind waves will interact with a
building west-northwest long period swell.

* WHERE...The beaches of Douglas, Coos, and Curry counties.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Sneaker waves can run up significantly farther on
beaches than normal, including over rocks and jetties. These
waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and sweep
them into the ocean. The waves can also move logs or other
objects which could crush or trap anyone caught underneath.

* View the hazard area in detail at
https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:

remain out of the water to avoid hazardous conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Washington, UT
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 9:11PM MDT until October 12 at 12:15AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Forsyth burn scar in...
Central Washington County in southwestern Utah...

* Until 1215 AM MDT.

* At 911 PM MDT, Emergency management reported flooding in Pine
Valley and high flows on the Santa Clara River above Baker
Reservoir from earlier rainfall. Between 1.50 and 3.50 inches of
rain have fallen since 9 AM. Flash flooding is ongoing. Excessive
rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow. The debris
flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Forsyth Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Forsyth Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Pine Valley.

This includes Utah Route 18 between mile markers 26 and 27.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Forsyth Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 12:15 AM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 12:15 AM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.
